doc.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024

title: Paris jam sessions
summary: Jam sessions remain conservative and standards-based; young groups play originals.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: If you went to a jam session in Paris is it old fashioned to say, “All right, let’s do a blues in B flat”?

No but that’s the other part of it. The older I get, the harder it is for me to leave the house. If I’m home I’d rather just stay home and practice or compose, so I’m not out as much. But if I’m already out and it’s close to the time when the sessions are going to start, the jam sessions are still pretty conservative though, to answer your question. And it depends on the night, it depends who’s there, the level could be, there could be a couple of great players and a couple of less experienced players, so kind of the common ground is still let’s play “Stella” or let’s play a standard. So when you go out to a jam session it’s not really the kind of experimental stuff I was talking about earlier. But it’s more if you’re going to go hear a young French group play their music it’s going to be more originals and something a little less beboppy for lack of a better term.
